title: All night on the mountain (Luke 6:1–16)
hookLine: before choosing the twelve, he prays all night

lines: HOW DO YOU MAKE A BIG CHOICE?
HE LEAVES THE NOISE AND CLIMBS.
cards: How do you make a choice that will shape everything after it? A job, a move, who to trust. Some people make lists, some ask friends, some lie awake at three in the morning, scrolling.
Luke shows Jesus making one: picking the small group who would carry his work after him.
The chapter starts with arguments: disciples picking grain on the sabbath, a man with a withered hand healed in a synagogue, tempers rising over what the sabbath is for.
Jesus asks: is it lawful on the sabbath to do good, or to do evil? Then, before the choice, he leaves the noise behind and climbs.

teach.h: HE CONTINUED ALL NIGHT IN PRAYER.
teach.b: In the King James words: "And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God." All night. Hours in the dark, on a hillside, alone.

teach.h: LUKE'S JESUS PRAYS AT THE TURNS.
teach.b: Luke keeps showing Jesus at prayer: at his baptism, in lonely places, before Peter names him the Christ, on another mountain before his face changes. In Luke, prayer turns up at the turning points.
Then: "And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles." The Greek is apostolos, someone sent out, an envoy.
Twelve, and many readers hear an echo of the twelve tribes of Israel.

teach.h: JUDAS TOO, AFTER A NIGHT OF PRAYER.
teach.b: Luke gives the names: Simon, whom he named Peter, and Andrew his brother; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew; Matthew and Thomas; James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called the Zealot; Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, "which also was the traitor."

teach.h: HE CONTINUED ALL NIGHT IN PRAYER TO GOD.
teach.b: A whole night of prayer, and the list still includes the man who will betray him. Luke doesn't explain that, and doesn't try. What the text does show: praying first didn't guarantee an easy outcome.
In Luke's telling, the choice was made in prayer, eyes open, at dawn.

how: Christians often pray before major decisions, and some keep a night or a day of prayer before an important choice, remembering Jesus' night on the mountain.

games.q: you have to choose the twelve people who will carry your life's work. the night before, what do you do?
o: go up a mountain and pray all night.
games.why: he prays through the night on a mountain, and at daybreak calls his disciples and chooses twelve.

practice: Bring to mind a decision in front of you, and don't solve it or run the pros and cons again; just hold it, the way you'd hold a stone in your hand, feeling its weight, what you fear and what you hope.
Let the quiet do some of the work the lists can't. If you pray, you can bring the choice to God without asking for an answer yet; if you don't, simply hold it in silence and see what rises.

wordCard.voice: Apostolos, Greek for one who is sent out, an envoy: the name Jesus gives the twelve, chosen at dawn after he prayed through the night alone on a hillside.

carryVoice: Your line: pray first. Even a whole night of prayer didn't make the road easy. Rest well, and see you tomorrow.
